source: Beaty, Benedek, Kaufman, Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
finding: Design: fMRI during Alternate Uses (create) versus Object Characteristics (control) with a 12 s idea period, to test whether default and executive networks cooperate in creative thought.
numbers: 28 recruited, 25 analysed (3 excluded for motion >3 mm); 13 women, age 18-30; 46 trials, 12 s generation, 3 s response; 3T, TR 2 s. Out-of-scanner brick AUT scored by 3 raters, alpha .87.
limits: Small sample. The control task (typical properties) is a weak match for creative demand. The creativity score came from a separate session, not from the scanned trials.
agent_relevance: Gives the paradigm behind the generate-loosely-then-control story. The idea period is split into early and late windows.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Kaufman, Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
finding: Whole-brain connectivity (MVPA) found a distributed divergent-thinking network spanning default (left precuneus, right PCC, bilateral inferior parietal), executive (right DLPFC) and salience (right ACC, bilateral insula) hubs, plus bilateral middle temporal gyri (memory retrieval).
numbers: MVPA threshold p<.001 voxelwise uncorrected; seed analyses p<.05 FWE cluster; ROI-to-ROI p<.05 FDR.
limits: MVPA is an omnibus test. Network labels depend on ROI placement, so the authors checked them in an independent sample.
agent_relevance: Three roles in one task: retrieval (temporal and default), control (DLPFC), switching (insula).

source: Beaty, Benedek, Kaufman, Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
finding: A resting-state check in an independent sample showed the PCC and precuneus seeds were anticorrelated with DLPFC, parietal executive regions, insula and ACC at rest, yet these same hubs coupled during creative generation. So the default-executive opposition seen at rest reverses in this task.
numbers: Independent age-matched resting sample n=42, 5 min eyes closed, band-pass .008-.09.
limits: Different people from the task sample. The authors argue the antagonism may be an artifact of tasks that need external attention.
agent_relevance: Supports the claim that cooperation is task-dependent. Our scaffold can treat generation and control as cooperating, not as exclusive modes.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Kaufman, Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
finding: Time course: the PCC coupled with bilateral insula in the first windows, then with right DLPFC, ACC and temporal regions in windows 2-4. DLPFC showed no coupling with default regions in windows 1-2, then coupled with PCC and right IPL in window 3. Nothing significant in the last window.
numbers: Five usable 2 s windows (TRs 2-6) of a 12 s period; FDR p<.05.
quote: default and salience coupling at the beginning, followed by default and executive coupling at later stages
limits: Windows are coarse because of BOLD lag. The ordering is inferred from connectivity differences, not causal flow. Reading the insula as a switch is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Best direct neural support for a two-phase order: salience-led start, control joins later. Suggests control should come after raw generation has begun, not before.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Kaufman, Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
finding: Individual differences: global efficiency of the divergent-thinking network correlated with rated creativity of out-of-scanner AUT responses.
limits: Single sample, no replication in the paper. p=.02 with n=25 is fragile; the effect-size inflation problem applies (see the Marek 2022 line).
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that efficient integration across networks, not the strength of any one network, goes with creative ability.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Wilkins, Jauk, Fink, Silvia, Hodges, Koschutnig, Neubauer (2014) Creativity and the default network: a functional connectivity analysis of the creative brain at rest
finding: Resting-state study: people with high divergent-thinking ability had stronger coupling between inferior frontal gyrus (executive) and default regions than low-ability people.
numbers: High n=12, low n=12 (top and bottom third of 91, matched on IQ 115.8 vs 106.8 p=.203, openness, age, gender). Left IFG with left IPL t=3.00 p=.008; PCC t=3.34 p=.005; right IPL t=3.75 p=.004; mPFC t=2.38 p=.026. Right IFG with left IPL t=2.76, right IPL t=3.36. DT composite 2.27 vs 1.88, p<.001.
limits: Extreme-group design, 24 people. Right IFG to mPFC/PCC did not differ even uncorrected. The 9-point IQ gap was non-significant but not zero. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Control-network coupling to the default system is a trait-like feature of good idea generators, not only a state during the task.

source: Benedek, Jauk, Fink, Koschutnig, Reishofer, Ebner, Neubauer (2014) To create or to recall? Neural mechanisms underlying the generation of creative new ideas
finding: Self-paced overt idea generation in fMRI separated new ideas from old (recalled) ideas. New ideas came later, took longer and were rated more creative.
numbers: Mean 85.37 ideas per person (SD 31.34). Old 48.34 vs new 37.02, F(1,102)=8.69. Latency old 6.69 s vs new 8.73 s, t(34)=6.83, d=1.16 (df 34 implies about 35 people). New rated more creative t(34)=8.66, d=1.46. Old ideas dominate the first 15 s.
quote: The beginning of the task was dominated by old ideas, but new ideas became more frequent at later stages
limits: Old versus new coding was by the participants. Only 46% of ideas were usable after the timing filter.
agent_relevance: Direct behavioural support for obvious-first, novel-later. Early outputs are mostly recalled, so a scaffold should push past the first wave.

source: Benedek, Jauk, Fink, Koschutnig, Reishofer, Ebner, Neubauer (2014) To create or to recall? Neural mechanisms underlying the generation of creative new ideas
finding: Fronto-parietal results: divergent thinking activated left IFG/SFG and right hippocampus and deactivated right TPJ, precuneus and PCC (default regions). New versus old ideas raised left inferior parietal cortex; orbital IFG activity rose with idea creativity.
numbers: Left IPC percent signal change 0.20 for new vs 0.07 for old; peak (-51,-34,40), t=4.24, k=29. FWE p<.05 whole brain for the main contrast. No region was stronger for old than new.
quote: a state of focused internally-directed attention involving controlled semantic retrieval
limits: Default deactivation here conflicts with a simple default-network-drives-generation story. The authors read it as focused internal attention with controlled semantic retrieval.
agent_relevance: Competing account: creative generation as controlled, internally focused retrieval. Inhibition of the dominant response (orbital IFG) tracks quality.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Silvia, Schacter (2016) Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics. Trends in Cognitive Sciences
finding: The founding model: the default network produces candidate ideas from memory, the control network evaluates and modifies them to fit the goal. Built on goal-directed self-generated thought (like autobiographical planning). Explicitly not a blind-variation, selective-retention theory.
numbers: About 50 cited sources; no new data. Default-control cooperation reported for divergent thinking, music, poetry, visual art.
quote: the default network influences the generation of candidate ideas, but that the control network can constrain and direct this process
limits: Review by the group that made the main studies. Insight is excluded. The generation-evaluation split is tested mainly in art tasks.
agent_relevance: Core justification for a two-phase scaffold: loose generation, then constrained evaluation. Note it is a coupling model, not a strict sequence.

source: Beaty, Benedek, Silvia, Schacter (2016) Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics. Trends in Cognitive Sciences
finding: The review reads the early default-salience coupling as the insula acting as a switch that enables later default-control coupling.
numbers: Based on one study (Beaty 2015, N=25) plus the salience-network switching literature.
limits: Inference from one small sample. Heinonen 2016 (n=16) also found left anterior insula, a small independent hint.
agent_relevance: Suggests a cheap switch signal (a detector that says when to hand over from generation to control) rather than a timer.

source: Liu, Erkkinen, Healey, Xu, Swett, Chow, Braun (2015) Brain activity and connectivity during poetry composition: toward a multidimensional model of the creative process
finding: Poetry composition: dorsolateral and parietal executive systems were attenuated during generation and re-engaged during revision, while medial prefrontal cortex was active in both. Experts deactivated DLPFC/IPS more during generation.
numbers: 27 people: 14 expert poets and 13 novices. The executive-default cluster correlation was negative during generation and reversed during revision (P<.01). Six tasks including memorized-recitation controls.
quote: cognitive control is attenuated during generation and re-engaged during revision
limits: Typed poems on a keyboard in a scanner. Experts and novices showed similar overall patterns. Phases were separate blocks, not free alternation.
agent_relevance: Best direct support for suspend control, then re-engage it. Experts suspend control more strongly: an argument for an explicit loose phase.

source: Ellamil, Dobson, Beeman, Christoff (2012) Evaluative and generative modes of thought during the creative process
finding: Book-cover design with alternating generation and evaluation. Generation preferentially recruited the medial temporal lobe; evaluation recruited executive and default regions together, plus rostrolateral PFC, insula and temporopolar cortex. Executive and default regions were positively connected throughout.
numbers: Numbers not read (abstract only).
limits: Abstract only. Challenges the simple map default = generate, control = evaluate: here generation was medial temporal, and cooperation held in both phases.
agent_relevance: Warns against hard-coding one network per phase. Evaluation is best modelled as combined control and intuitive appraisal.

source: Beaty, Christensen, Benedek, Silvia, Schacter (2017/2018) Creative constraints: brain activity and network dynamics underlying semantic interference during idea production. NeuroImage
finding: Behavioural result: after studying noun-verb pairs, asking people to think creatively of a verb for a studied noun (high constraint, strong prepotent answer) lowered the semantic distance of responses compared with unstudied nouns.
numbers: N=24 analysed (26 recruited). Recall 76% test 1, 94% test 2. Semantic distance (LSA) low-constraint M=.76 (SD .03) vs high-constraint M=.74 (SD .05); t(21)=2.12, p=.04.
limits: Tiny effect (0.02 on a distance scale), p just under .05, 22 usable. Single lab.
agent_relevance: A measured cost of a strong obvious answer: it pulls ideas toward it. Supports inhibit-the-obvious as a step.

source: Beaty, Christensen, Benedek, Silvia, Schacter (2017/2018) Creative constraints: brain activity and network dynamics underlying semantic interference during idea production. NeuroImage
finding: Imaging result: the interference condition raised default (PCC, angular gyri), salience (right anterior insula) and left DLPFC activity, and increased coupling of anterior default with left executive network. Low-constraint minus high-constraint showed nothing.
numbers: High>Low constraint: precuneus cluster survived FWE; DLPFC, PCC, bilateral angular, right insula only at p<.001 uncorrected. ICA networks: anterior default plus left executive higher in high-constraint.
limits: Mostly uncorrected threshold, N=24. The mechanism claim (control network inhibits the default-retrieved answer) is inferred.
agent_relevance: Mechanistic hint for a step: retrieve the dominant answer, mark it, then search away from it.

source: Madore, Thakral, Beaty, Addis, Schacter (2019) Neural mechanisms of episodic retrieval support divergent creative thinking. Cerebral Cortex
finding: An episodic specificity induction (brief training in recalling details) raised hippocampal activity and coupling between a core episodic network and a frontoparietal control network during divergent thinking, and the coupling extended to a later rest scan. Behaviourally it raised idea production on divergent thinking but not on object association.
numbers: Numbers not read (abstract only).
limits: Abstract only. Behavioural effects were on idea production, not necessarily on overall quality.
agent_relevance: A concrete prompt lever: ask the model to recall specific detailed episodes before generating uses. Cheap to test.

source: Beaty, Kenett, Christensen, Rosenberg, Benedek, Chen, Fink, Qiu, Kwapil, Kane, Silvia (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity. PNAS
finding: Connectome-based predictive modelling of AUT creativity from task fMRI. A high-creative network (224 positive edges) predicted creativity; a low-creative network (603 negative edges) did so less well. Top hubs included default, salience and executive regions.
numbers: Training N=163, leave-one-out, 268-node atlas, 35,778 possible edges, edge threshold p<.01. High network r(161)=.30, P=1.3e-4 (permutation P .001). Low network r=.22, P=.004 (permutation .019). Control task (object characteristics): high r=.05 ns, low r=.19.
limits: Effects are modest (r around .3, about 9% of variance). The two networks did not differ significantly. Top-25 hubs: 12 default, 4 salience, 3 executive.
agent_relevance: Brain connectivity is a modest biomarker. Default hubs dominate; control hubs are present but fewer.

source: Beaty et al. (2018) PNAS: external replication
finding: The high-creative network generalised to three independent samples, but the low-creative network replicated only in the resting-state sample and in an unexpected direction.
numbers: High network: external 1 (n=39) r(37)=.35 P=.03; external 2 (n=54) r(52)=.28 P=.03; external 3 (n=405, Chinese rest data) r(403)=.13 P=.008. Low network: r=-.04, .02, .11 (only the last significant, P=.03).
limits: The effect shrinks from r=.35 and .28 in small samples to .13 in n=405, which matches the inflation pattern of small samples. Different tasks across samples.
agent_relevance: Expect a real effect near r=.1 to .15; do not build the scaffold on a claim of large neural effects.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition: mapping cognitive mechanisms and individual differences in the creative brain. Curr Opin Behav Sci
finding: The key 2019 review links network interactions to three cognitive mechanisms: goal-directed memory retrieval (executive-default), prepotent-response inhibition (executive-default), and internally focused attention (executive-visual). Its own framing: default network involved in idea generation, executive network guiding, constraining and modifying.
numbers: Table 1 lists ten correlational studies from 2017-2018 with N from 22 to 1,277 (e.g. Takeuchi N=1,277; Sun N=574; Kenett N=416; Zhu N=282). Right posterior IPL coupled with visual cortex under internal attention. No effect sizes reported in the review.
quote: with DN involved in idea generation and ECN in guiding, constraining, and modifying DN processes
limits: Mostly correlational. No formal two-phase or sequential model; it is a division of labour. The review says causality is untested and suggests tACS.
agent_relevance: Names three operations our scaffold could mirror: targeted retrieval, suppressing the obvious, shielding attention from distraction.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition (dynamics and individual-difference section)
finding: Dynamic-connectivity studies: high divergent thinkers switch between connectivity states more often. High openness is linked to more time in a state where default, salience, executive and dorsal attention networks correlate positively. Of 13 networks, only default within-network variability tracked verbal creativity. Lesion work: medial prefrontal (default) damage impaired remote concept generation; left rostrolateral PFC (executive) damage spared generation but impaired combination.
numbers: Lesion study 29 frontal patients vs 54 controls; two matched-group studies of 22 high vs 22 low. Longitudinal: executive network grey-matter maturation tracked divergent thinking 3 years later.
limits: Sex differences appear in structural studies. Figural vs verbal and rest vs task give different networks.
agent_relevance: Flexibility of switching between modes matters, not only the amount of control. Lesion data (causal for humans) split generation (default) from combination (control).

source: Mayseless, Eran, Shamay-Tsoory (2015) Generating original ideas: the neural underpinning of originality
finding: Original ideas went with activity in default regions (mPFC, PCC). More original people had stronger ventral ACC activity, coupled with left occipitotemporal cortex. Authors tie it to a dual model: a generation system and a control system.
numbers: 30 people scanned (from abstract).
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Independent group supporting generation-plus-control, with the ACC as the control hub.

source: Heinonen, Numminen, Hlushchuk, Antell, Taatila, Suomala (2016) Default mode and executive networks areas: association with the serial order in divergent thinking. PLoS One
finding: Silent (non-spoken) alternative-uses generation activated the left anterior insula against object identification. Activity in ACC (executive) and default regions (precuneus, IPL, PCC) rose with the serial order of the idea.
numbers: n=16 (abstract).
limits: Abstract only, small n. The serial order effect fits Benedek's later-ideas-are-newer result.
agent_relevance: Later ideas need more of both networks. Argues for sampling past the first outputs and costing them more.

source: Wu, Yang, Tong, Sun, Chen, Wei, Zhang, Zhang, Qiu (2015) A meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies on divergent thinking using activation likelihood estimation
finding: ALE meta-analysis: the divergent thinking network covers lateral PFC, posterior parietal (IPL, precuneus), ACC and temporal regions. Left DLPFC is linked to selecting remote associates; ACC to forming distant associations; many regions were deactivated.
numbers: Counts not read (abstract only).
limits: Abstract only. Reverse inference from regions to function is loose. Studies pooled use different tasks.
agent_relevance: Meta-level support that frontal control and parietal/temporal memory regions co-occur.

source: Dietrich and Kanso (2010) A review of EEG, ERP, and neuroimaging studies of creativity and insight. Psychological Bulletin
finding: Critical baseline: across 72 experiments in 63 articles, divergent-thinking neuroimaging showed no reliable changes beyond diffuse prefrontal activation. Creative thinking was not tied to any single process or region, nor to defocused attention.
numbers: 72 experiments, 63 articles.
limits: Abstract only. Predates the network-connectivity work, which was partly a response.
agent_relevance: A competing view to keep: defocused attention is not supported. The loose and controlled stages are not a single dial.

source: Marek et al. (2022) Reproducible brain-wide association studies require thousands of individuals. Nature
finding: Brain-wide association effects are smaller than thought; at typical sample sizes they are underpowered, inflated and often fail to replicate. Reproducibility improves into the thousands, with fMRI, cognitive tests and multivariate methods giving more robust effects.
numbers: About 50,000 people across three datasets; median neuroimaging study n about 25.
limits: Abstract only. The creativity studies above use n=12 to 163; these fall in the unreliable range.
agent_relevance: Treat the n=24-25 coupling findings as hypotheses. Large-sample ones (n=163, 405, 1,277) are the better anchor.

source: Ismayilzada, Luchini, Gokce, AlKhamissi, Bosselut, Laverghetta, van der Plas, Beaty (2026) Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking. COLM 2026 (arXiv 2604.03480)
finding: First test of LLM-brain alignment during active creative thinking. Used the Beaty 2018 fMRI data (170 participants, AUT and OCT) with representational similarity in default (DMN), frontoparietal (FPN) and somatomotor control networks. Models 270M-72B.
numbers: 170 people, 8 removed in cleaning; 46 stimuli, about 23 per task each. At the early cue stage, DMN alignment correlates with model size r=0.55 (p<.05) and AUT score r=0.52 (p<.05).
quote: larger and more creatively capable models more closely mirror the neural representations underlying human divergent thinking
limits: Correlational (representational similarity), p<.05 across a modest set of models. The size and AUT-score correlations come from different token pooling methods (last-token vs mean). Taking the max over layers gives an optimistic upper bound. Header says COLM 2026.
agent_relevance: Evidence that bigger models resemble the brain's creative state at the prompt stage, but this concerns representation, not a scaffold.

source: Ismayilzada, Luchini, Gokce, AlKhamissi, Bosselut, Laverghetta, van der Plas, Beaty (2026) Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking. COLM 2026 (arXiv 2604.03480)
finding: Stage dependence: alignment links to size and AUT score at the prompt stage but weakens once the model generates a response. Across families the link weakens; within the Gemma-3 family the size and AUT correlations stay positive at the response stage.
numbers: Correlations with size and performance weaken after generation (appendix figures); generation length is not correlated with DMN alignment.
limits: Family heterogeneity can explain the loss. The authors offer two readings: models converge on similar answers, or outputs diverge from human outputs with scale.
agent_relevance: The model's state while reading the problem looks more brain-like than its written ideas. Suggests shaping the prompt-stage step (framing) and then controlling output.

source: Ismayilzada, Luchini, Gokce, AlKhamissi, Bosselut, Laverghetta, van der Plas, Beaty (2026) Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking. COLM 2026 (arXiv 2604.03480)
finding: Post-training: a creativity-optimised Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (CrPO) keeps alignment with high-creativity human responses but loses the positive alignment with low-creativity ones; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B shows negative alignment with high-creativity responses. Partly generalises: R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B show positive low-creativity alignment.
numbers: Rating cutoff 2.0 (also 1.75, 2.25). CrPO-SFT and CrPO-DPO, same data, both keep low-creativity alignment, so only the full method differs. The text gives signs and leans, no single effect size.
limits: Single seeds, two model families. The authors say associated with, not caused by.
agent_relevance: Reasoning-chain training may cost creative representation. A scaffold that adds a chain of reasoning to every step could reduce divergent output; keep loose generation separate from verification.

source: Wenger and Kenett (2025) We're different, we're the same: creative homogeneity across LLMs. arXiv 2501.19361
finding: Across many LLMs, creative answers were far more similar to each other than human answers were to each other, even when individual originality matched or beat humans.
numbers: AUT originality: LLM 0.711 vs human 0.695 (t(2094)=-3.4, p=.001). Within-group variability (semantic distance): LLM 0.459 vs human 0.738 (t(10078)=19.1, p=3.9e-80). A very-creative system prompt raised LLM originality to 0.754 and variability to 0.576, still below humans.
quote: LLM responses are much more similar to other LLM responses than human responses are to each other
limits: Different tests (AUT, Forward Flow, DAT). Embeddings define similarity. Not a brain study; it measures the output side of generation. Column reading is from a text-extracted table.
agent_relevance: Single-model loose generation is not diverse; a scaffold needs real sources of variety (different framings, code-checked novelty filters), not just a be-creative instruction.

source: Synthesis for the agent: what network neuroscience licenses (Angle A)
finding: Reading the sources together: support is strongest for (1) obvious answers come first and cost control to get past (Benedek 2014, Beaty 2018 constraints), (2) control engages later in the window (Beaty 2015) and re-engages for revision (Liu 2015), (3) cooperation not opposition. It is weakest for a clean one-network-per-phase map (Ellamil 2012 contradicts it).
numbers: Sample sizes behind the temporal-order claim: 25 (Beaty 2015), 27 (Liu 2015), about 35 (Benedek 2014), 24 (Beaty 2018 constraints).
limits: Conclusion drawn by me from the lines above; neural data cannot show that a text scaffold works. Reverse inference risk.
agent_relevance: Fits SCHEMA principles: loose generation then code-checked control; signal-triggered handover (insula-like switch) rather than a schedule. No evidence here for forced doubt on a timer.
